skill.name: gitops-workflow
skill.description: Guides Kubernetes GitOps workflows with ArgoCD and Flux, including repository layout, sync policies, progressive delivery, and secret management.
skill.summary: Implement Kubernetes GitOps workflows with ArgoCD, Flux, sync policies, and safer promotion patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings were Markdown fences, placeholder URLs, or declarative YAML examples and were dismissed. Confirmed risks center on remote install content, sudo execution, and cluster-mutating commands that require explicit review. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote Flux installer is downloaded and executed with sudo.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a version, verify checksums or signatures, and prefer package-manager installation before any privileged execution.

remediation.issue: Remote Kubernetes install manifests are applied directly from URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Use version-pinned manifests and instruct users to inspect or vendor the manifest before applying it to a cluster.

remediation.issue: The ArgoCD repository example passes a token on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Use credential helpers, environment variables, or secret references, and warn about shell history and process-list exposure.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting examples include prune and force sync commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add approval, diff review, and rollback checks before commands that delete or overwrite cluster resources.

The Helm repository URL is a normal ArgoCD installation source. It is kept as a low-risk finding because it pulls installation content from the network.
The GitHub URL is a placeholder repository endpoint in setup documentation, not a suspicious exfiltration host. The separate token handling risk is captured as a semantic finding.
The URL is a placeholder repository value in an ArgoCD create command. There is no fixed third-party destination or hidden network behavior.
The Kubernetes default service URL is an internal cluster API endpoint used by ArgoCD examples. It is not an external network destination.

content.value_statement: Kubernetes deployment workflows drift when changes are applied outside Git. This skill guides GitOps setup with ArgoCD, Flux, sync policies, and safer promotion patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains OpenGitOps principles and when GitOps is appropriate.
Shows ArgoCD installation, application definitions, and App of Apps layout.
Shows Flux bootstrap, GitRepository resources, and Kustomization resources.
Documents automated sync, retry behavior, and sync windows.
Includes examples for canary, blue-green, External Secrets, and Sealed Secrets.
Lists troubleshooting commands for ArgoCD sync and diff checks.
limitations: Does not validate cluster access, repository permissions, or cloud IAM settings.
Example commands require review before use in production clusters.
Uses placeholder repository URLs, namespaces, and organization names.
Does not replace environment-specific security review for secrets or deployment approvals.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a GitOps Platform
use_cases.description: Set up initial ArgoCD or Flux workflows for Kubernetes deployments.

use_cases.title: Standardize Application Delivery
use_cases.description: Define repository layout, sync behavior, and promotion paths for application teams.

use_cases.title: Plan Controlled Production Sync
use_cases.description: Review approval gates, rollback paths, and secret handling before production automation.

prompt_templates.title: Check GitOps Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether GitOps fits my Kubernetes deployment process. Ask for missing cluster, repository, and approval details first.

prompt_templates.title: Design Repo Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitOps repository layout for staging and production. Include ownership, promotion flow, and rollback considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Delivery Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose ArgoCD or Flux for my cluster. Compare setup steps, sync behavior, secrets, and operations tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned GitOps production workflow for unsafe automation. Focus on pruning, force sync, secrets, approvals, and recovery steps.

output_examples.input: Help me choose ArgoCD or Flux for a small platform team.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of tool fit, setup effort, repository model, sync behavior, and operational tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Review our production sync plan before we enable automation.
output: Approval gates should protect production changes.
Prune and force sync need documented rollback steps.
Secret handling should avoid cleartext values in Git.

output_examples.input: Plan a GitOps rollout path for a new application.
output_examples.output: A staged delivery plan covering repository structure, environment promotion, health checks, and rollback expectations.

best_practices: Review remote manifests and installer scripts before applying them to a cluster.
Keep production sync behind approval gates and tested promotion paths.
Use External Secrets or Sealed Secrets instead of storing cleartext secrets in Git.
anti_patterns: Running downloaded installers with elevated privileges without verifying the source.
Using one repository path for every environment without clear ownership or review.
Enabling auto-sync with prune in production before rollback and alerting are tested.

faq.question: Does this skill install ArgoCD or Flux automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example commands that users must review before running.

faq.question: Does it support both ArgoCD and Flux?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers setup concepts, repository sources, sync policies, and common workflow patterns for both tools.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Kubernetes?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is focused on Kubernetes-based GitOps delivery.

faq.question: Does it cover secret management?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes External Secrets and Sealed Secrets patterns for keeping cleartext secrets out of Git.

faq.question: Are the commands safe for unattended agents?
faq.answer: No. Cluster-changing and privileged commands need explicit review, least privilege access, and environment checks.

faq.question: Does it include progressive delivery guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes canary and blue-green deployment examples for controlled rollouts.
